messages:
simon: Heads-up — customer today ran into a weird state where a runtime guard blocked traffic but the console showed the rollout at 100%. Who owns the flag vs rollout policy precedence? :thinking:

alex: Ugh we keep getting these. Short answer: we don't have a clear source-of-truth. Console edits apply to 'rollout config' but runtime has guard checks that can be pushed from infra. Problem is we don't expose that origin in the UI or API.

maria: We should add a small 'source' field everywhere (console/runtime/ops) and display it in the rollout timeline. Also, if runtime-created guards exist, they should probably take precedence for safety.

jen: Agree on the 'source' field. For API semantics I'm thinking: immutable when source==runtime unless ops explicitly reassigns ownership. Example (pseudo):
```json
GET /api/rollouts/:id -> {
  "id": "r123",
  "split": 0.5,
  "source": "runtime",
  "owner": "infra-team",
  "editable": false
}
```
That way console knows to show a lock/readonly state.

kumar: How does this affect telemetry and dashboards? If runtime silently overrides traffic, product teams will be confused. We should annotate trace logs and per-request metadata with `policy_source` and `policy_version` so the Console and Cost dashboards can show why a request was routed differently.

alex: +1 on policy annotations. For UX: show a little :lock: icon and hover text "Managed by runtime (safety guard) — contact infra to change". Also add a CTA "Request change" which creates a ticket with audit context.

simon: Another edge: experiments need 'shadow flags' where console-run experiments can mirror traffic but must not affect safety guards. I think prioritization should be: guard checks (runtime) > routing policy (runtime) > console rollouts (experiments). We need a short precedence matrix.

maria: Can we also support a merge rule instead of binary precedence? Eg, console says split 20% to variant A, runtime guard reduces to 5% because of quota. Merge result should be deterministic and visible. Small rule: final_split = runtime_min(console_split, runtime_cap) is easy to explain.

jen: That merge rule sounds reasonable. We should document a few deterministic combination rules (min, max, multiplier) and let runtime advertise which strategy it used in the rollout status. Example response fragment for the UI: 
```json
{
  "id": "r123",
  "console_split": 0.2,
  "runtime_cap": 0.05,
  "effective_split": 0.05,
  "resolution_strategy": "runtime_cap_min_console"
}
```

kumar: For dashboards: show both console_split and effective_split historically with a note about resolution_strategy. Also add alerting on large deltas (console vs effective) so PMs know when infra is throttling experiments.

alex: Operationally, we need ACLs: who can mark a config source as runtime, who can reassign ownership. Also migration plan for existing flags — we should backfill source=console for current ones, then have infra set source=runtime where they push guards.

simon: Can we get a small iteration plan? I propose: (1) quick API + UI change to display source and lock state, (2) telemetry annotation in proxy so we can show effective_split and source in dashboards, (3) RFC for precedence/migration. I'll take RFC. Maria can own dashboards, Jen API changes, Alex will do UI affordances.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rollout-source-annotations -> staging at 2026-03-19T15:40:00Z :rocket:

simon: Great — thanks all. I'll draft the RFC and ping infra for a list of current runtime guards so we can plan backfill. :+1:
